channel.title: Via blog
channel.description: We're making Via better every day! Subscribe to keep up to date with our progress.

item.title: Wyvern, a Snapdragon module on one flat board
item.description: Wyvern is a Snapdragon development board laid out like a Teensy. A Qualcomm QCS6490 module, which runs Linux or Android, shares the board with an RP2350 microcontroller on 30 pins.

item.title: Signet, a mouse worn as a ring of flat boards
item.description: Signet is a computer mouse you wear as a ring on your index finger. It's made of eight small circuit boards that sit around the finger, each one soldered to the next along an edge.

item.title: Rosetta, a controller whose knob picks the console
item.description: Rosetta is one game controller for a PS4, a PS5, an Xbox, a Switch or anything over Bluetooth. You pick the console with a five-position knob that sits where an Xbox 360 pad has its guide button.

item.title: Lark, a voice-controlled ceiling-fan bulb on four boards
item.description: Lark is a ceiling-fan light bulb designed for voice control, with the speech recognition running inside the bulb. It screws into the fan's E26 socket and runs on 120 V mains.

item.title: Hush, a speaker that plays the inverse of what it hears
item.description: Hush is a ring-shaped circuit board that sits on the face of a 40 mm speaker. A microphone on its hub picks up the noise in front of the cone, and the speaker plays the opposite of that noise.

item.title: Basalt: fitting a Threadripper onto a microATX board
item.description: Basalt is a motherboard for AMD's Threadripper 7000 and 9000 processors, on a microATX board 244 mm square.

item.title: Herald: answering a fire panel's phone call in firmware
item.description: Herald is a board that sits beside a fire alarm panel and passes its reports on. Many panels report by dialing a monitoring station over a phone line.
